speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to help me determine the cause, can you describe exactly what the dizziness feels like, such as a spinning sensation or just feeling lightheaded?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the spinning sensation and improvement with diphenhydramine suggest a vestibular origin. You mentioned increasing garlic intake for a cold; can you confirm if you also developed a rash or difficulty breathing, or did the garlic consumption happen without any allergic symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis. The clinical picture of constant vertigo, nausea, and a recent viral illness (cold) without mention of hearing loss or auditory symptoms points to inflammation of the vestibular nerve rather than labyrinthitis or Meniere's disease.
